expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: If you can find the cap room, Allen is a tremendous foundation for lineups. His rushing upside means you don't even need to stack him with his pass catchers. In 3 games, he already has 28 rushes for 114 yards and 6 touchdowns. He won't keep that pace up every week, but this team has to score a ton. The offense is elite and the defense is terrible, which is exactly the recipe you want. The matchup isn't pretty on paper, but Allen's history against the Patriots says otherwise, with 20+ fantasy points in 5 of the last 6 meetings.

players.notes: Elite rushing floor and elite offense in a 49.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Highest total on the slate. Trevor Lawrence is mispriced. Not afraid to use his legs as well. Safe cash QB this week.

players.notes: Highest game total on the slate at 51.5 points.
Solid 17.46 projection with a 42.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: It turns out the best QB of our lifetimes is still a great fantasy football option, who would have thought? Mahomes only scored 16.5 fantasy points last week as the Dolphins were unable to push the Chiefs at all but I do think the Raiders as only 4.5 dogs should be able to get KC into the 30s in points scored.

players.notes: Raiders defense should push the Chiefs into high scoring.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Jaguars are allowing 8.8 yards per attempt this season despite facing some QBs who aren’t all that great. Burrow hasn’t had a huge game yet, but the Bengals also haven’t pushed the ball downfield much. His aDOT is just 6.7 yards this season, while opposing offenses have averaged a 10.04-yard aDOT against the Jaguars. I think that changes here. Cincinnati should be able to create explosive plays and push the pace of this game. You can double-stack Burrow with Chase and Higgins, but if I’m choosing one, I lean Chase.

players.notes: Favorable matchup against a secondary allowing 8.8 yards per attempt.
Strong 18.29 projection with a 48.5 game total.
Solid 20.13 projection with a 48.5 game total.
Solid 19.30 projection in a 48.5 game total matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Direct GPP pivot from Josh Allen, as Lamar Jackson is projected for a fraction of the ownership with a very high ceiling. Ravens implied for 3rd highest team total on the slate.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The Ravens have the single highest team total of the week behind the Bills, but absolutely no one is interested in playing this stack. The Titans actually look like they might be more of a pass funnel, with an above average run defense and a bottom 8 pass defense in EPA/play allowed. The Ravens offensive line is also dealing with some injuries that I think will make it tougher on Derrick Henry (despite the revenge angle), but Lamar's mobility and wizardry can withstand that. Lamar is so efficient that limited dropbacks are not a major issue, and he scored nearly 30 DK points week 1 with just 25 pass attempts. If the Titans can push the Ravens (who are 21st in defensive EPA/play), the ceiling is nuclear.

players.notes: Third highest implied team total on the slate.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Brissett was a fun story last year, but nobody expected him to keep it up in 2026. Not sure why we slept on him. He has elite weapons and a defense that lets up a bunch of points. Dating back to last season, he's topped 20 fantasy points in 10 of his last 15 games, which is great production at his price point. The matchup against the Giants is easy to like too, since they're 27th in EPA allowed per dropback and now missing one of their best EDGE rushers.

players.notes: Facing a Giants defense missing their top edge rusher.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: I typically would gloss over Stroud in DFS because the upside is so low, but this week he has two things working in his favor: a low price tag on both sites and a fantastic matchup against a Cowboys secondary that is working out guys off the street this week to come in and play a role due to the rash of injuries they have suffered over the last two weeks.

players.notes: Favorable matchup against an injury-ravaged Cowboys secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: I find it hard to believe his ownership stays this low, but if it is, he is an amazing GPP-play. Dolphins have allowed the most fantasy points to opposing RBs on both sites and Vikings just ruled out Justin Jefferson which means they should lean on Aaron Jones a little more on the ground. Dolphins have a allowed an astonishing 2.33 TDs per game to opposing RBs.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Aaron Jones gets the best possible matchup against the Dolphins and with Justin Jefferson out, they may lean on Jones for a few more carries.  He also saw 6 targets last game against TB and he is one of the top value plays on the slate on both sites.

players.notes: Expanded ground role with Justin Jefferson ruled out.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: We have plenty of great running back plays on this slate, but none compare to McCaffrey. There were rumblings that the Niners wanted to limit him this season, and that showed in the first 2 games. But in their first competitive game, he played 82% of the snaps against the Cardinals. This week, the Niners host the Broncos in a game with a 2.5-point spread. San Francisco is missing pieces in the passing game, and Denver is dead last in EPA against the run this season. CMC should see 15+ carries and potentially double-digit targets depending on the game script.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Broncos have allowed the 6th most DK FPPG and the 5th most FD FPPG to opposing RBs. 49ers have the 6th highest implied team total on the slate. CMC offers one of the safest floors on the slate and a cash RB priority.

players.notes: Heavy snap share facing Denver's last-ranked run defense.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Averaging over 25 fantasy points per game, Walker should be priced at least 10% higher on both DraftKings and Fanduel given his role at the goalline and in the passing game.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Walker has been elite in every way to start the season and he is getting all the touches in the KC offense.  He’s had 3 big games to start the season getting 23, 24 and 18 rushing attempts along with multiple goal line carries.  He’s is one of my top RB plays on the slate.

players.notes: Strong 20.37 projection with a 47.5 game total.
Strong 16.70 projection in a 51.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: New Ravens OC Declan Doyle has this running game humming with Henry. That, plus a revenge spot against the team that didn't want him anymore and Lamar Jackson actively looking to run less when he doesn't need to, makes me think Henry is as good a bet as anyone in the NFL for two-plus rushing touchdowns in any given matchup.

players.notes: High touchdown upside in a strong running scheme.
Solid 16.05 projection with a 43.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Breece Hall isn’t likely to play, and this Bears run defense has not been good. They’ve allowed 2.58 yards before contact per attempt, and if they’re giving Allen that kind of room to build up a full head of steam, he’s going to have multiple explosive runs in this game.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Braelon played every snap after Breece was hurt last week, and he had every RB opportunity, including 3 targets. The Bears are a total sieve in run defense, and he's far too cheap for the lead back role here.

players.notes: Expected lead workhorse role against a weak run defense.
Solid 14.72 projection with a 42.5 game total.
Solid 16.93 projection with a 47.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Top 5 in the NFL in target share, yards per route run, fantasy points per target and expected fantasy points. This is what a fantasy football superstar looks like.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Cash combo of TLaw + Parker Washington is very appealing. Like mentioned already with TLaw, Jaguars/Bengals implied for highest total on the slate. Bengals have faced some pretty mediocre receiving cores (Bucs, Texans without Nico Collins, and Steelers). Parker Washington is currently top 10 in Air Yard Share, target %, and Fantasy Points per route run. All advance stats that signal him to be a true #1 receiver.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Washington has been a staple of this article all season, and he's yet to let us down. He's cleared 90 receiving yards or found the end zone in all 3 games. The underlying usage says he should be even better, with a 28% target share and a 46% air yards share. What's more impressive is he's built those numbers while running almost half his routes from the slot. This game against the Bengals carries the highest total on the board this week.

players.notes: Elite 28% target share in the highest total game.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: I wouldn't let the Monday night game fool you. The Bears defense is not that good, despite Jalen Hurts making them look like the '85 Bears. Wilson is the most talented and most heavily targeted WR on this team, and he should find room against this secondary as long as his QB can get him the ball.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Without AD Mitchell in the lineup, we should reasonably expect Garrett Wilson to have a target share north of 30%.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Wilson got off to a slow start against the Lions, but a big game was never really in question; the spot was too good to fail. He finished with 10 catches for 107 yards and a touchdown. This week the Jets are missing Breece Hall, A.D. Mitchell, and Mason Taylor, which should leave their offense running through very few hands. Even better, they draw the Bears, who rarely bother playing defense.

players.notes: Expanded target share above 30% with teammates out.
Solid 14.03 projection with a 38.5 game total.
Top tier 22.69 projection on the slate.
Solid 11.77 projection in a 42.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Bengals haven’t had a 100-yard receiver this season, and I think that changes with Chase in this game. The Jaguars are allowing 8.8 yards per attempt this season despite facing some QBs who aren’t all that great. The only WR they’ve faced who is anywhere near Ja’Marr Chase’s level is Jaylen Waddle, and he finished with 138 receiving yards. Outside of Waddle, rookie Denzel Boston had 59 receiving yards, while Mack Hollins got up to 87. This is the Chase explosion game. He’s coming off a 14-reception, 165-yard performance against a better version of this Jaguars defense last season, and he did that with Jake Browning at QB.

players.notes: Top tier receiving upside in the highest total game.
Solid 17.66 projection with a 42.5 game total.
Solid 17.73 projection in a 48.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: With the Bucs blitzing at the 3rd highest rate in the league and a struggling OL, Watson's ability to catch and run give him the upside to break this slate. He's also the primary red zone target for the team, leading the Pack in both red zone and end zone targets, while improving his per route efficiency to elite levels (2.51 YPRR this season). If the Bucs can cobble together some points, Watson has as high of a ceiling as any WR at a reasonable price and low ownership.

players.notes: Elite red-zone role facing a heavy blitz defense.
Solid 14.97 projection with a 42.5 game total.
Solid 14.49 projection with a 47.5 game total.
Solid 12.91 projection in a 48.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Obviously, this is a great matchup in general terms these days, with the Dolphins being arguably the worst team in the NFL. This is a fantastic punt price on DraftKings for a tight end who could take on a bigger role in the offense this week.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Cheap on both sites and Vikings have ruled out Justin Jefferson opening up a bigger role for TJ Hockenson this weekend. Dolphins also have struggled to stop the TE position over the last few seasons, including this year, where they are bottom 10 vs the position. Hard to pass on the value, especially in cash games.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: He hasn't played a game without Justin Jefferson since 2023, but in 2023, Hockenson averaged 9.9 targets and 17.31 PPR FPPG without Jefferson, compared to 7.3 targets and 12.35 FPPG with Jefferson. He gets a great matchup this week against the Dolphins.

players.notes: Expanded target role with Justin Jefferson ruled out.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Bowers delivered as good a game as you could've hoped for in his return from injury: 10 catches for 116 yards and a touchdown. He's a tight end in name only; he lined up in the slot constantly and pulled in 39% of the team's targets. Think of him as a WR1 you get to play at tight end. With the Raiders likely trailing in this one, that target share should hold up. There's a ton of value out there this week, which makes spending up at tight end an easy call.

players.notes: Heavy slot alignment and a massive 39% target share.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: I think the 49ers are going to attack their former safety Talanoa Hufanga in coverage with George Kittle. The Rams had a lot of plays where a TE was running open against this defense, and Stafford missed quite a few of those opportunities. I expect Shanahan to take a lot from that game plan, and I think Purdy will find Kittle for a big game.

players.notes: Favorable seam matchup attacking the opposing secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: McBride always ends up too low-owned in DFS. Most people want to save at the position, so the pricier tight ends get passed over. With Bowers back in the mix this week, McBride might go even more overlooked than usual. He's commanding a 28% target share and a 27% air yards share in an offense that's quietly underrated. Stack him with Brissett, or go the skinny-stack route and pair him with Skattebo.

players.notes: Strong 28% target share in an underrated offense.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Kelce perfect GPP candidate with Raiders getting absolutely torched last week by the Saints TEs (combined 12-86-4), yet should be relatively on the lower owned side with a cash/value play like Hockenson available or pay-up guys like McBride/Bowers available. Based on the eye test, Kelce looks fresher and in-shape for this year where in 2025 you say some sort of dip.

players.notes: Favorable matchup against a defense struggling with tight ends.
Solid 11.05 projection with a 44.5 game total.
Solid 11.51 projection in a 49.5 game total.
Solid 10.55 projection with a 43.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Spending this much on a defense (specifically on DraftKings) never feels good, but the Vikings ($4,000 DK / $5,000 FD) are in a tremendous spot this week. They are massive favorites at home against the Dolphins, who have been one of the worst offensive teams in the NFL this season. The Vikings blitz more than any team, and they force the Dolphins into a pass-heavy game plan. Minnesota is also 1st in points allowed and EPA allowed per play. They could have a slate-breaking type of performance.
